points.heading: Deepen: choosing one or two words
points.body:
Today we use the week’s ideas to choose a Spanish verb form. A simple form has one word, such as «terminé». A compound form has haber and a participle, such as «he terminado». Start by deciding what the sentence wants to tell.

Ask three questions. Did the action end at a closed moment, such as yesterday at five? A form like «canté» fits. Did the action happen already and does its result matter now? A form like «he cantado» fits. Are you describing a past habit or background? A form like «cantaba» fits. In «Leía cuando llamaron», leía is the background and llamaron is the finished event.

The same verb can tell different stories. «Terminé ayer» closes the past, while «He terminado ya» connects a finished action to the present.

Practice: Write five sentences. For each one, try a one-word and a two-word version, then choose the version that matches your meaning and explain your choice.

Common mistake: Mixing the imperfect and preterite without deciding whether the action was background or finished.

lesson.summary: Choose a verb form by deciding whether the action is closed, still matters now, or forms a past background or habit.
